source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text:
I redeployed a new contract to resolve the ETH issue.
The Fix Implemented:
* Slippage tolerance is configurable (default: 85 = 15% slippage)
* The owner can adjust it through the setSwapSlippageTolerance() function
* ETH minting will now function even when markets are volatile

Steps Required to Go Live:
Configure Chainlink VRF:
* Visit vrf.chain.link
* Add this consumer: 0x339e73f5D77CA643ED4A39aA4Bc1DF5c6faACd9b

execution.observed_behavior: Freelancer reports deploying a replacement contract to address the ETH issue.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
It looks like your USDC mint came from a different mint contract, which is the contract that most of the site stats are now aligned with.
I'll prepare the chainlink stuff, but I won't make any changes until you wake up and confirm, because increasing slippage to 15% doesn't make any sense to me.

execution.observed_behavior: After the replacement deployment, the client observes that a USDC mint used a different contract and most site statistics became aligned with that different contract.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hmmmmm... yes, I do think that'd be the best approach.
I'm not particularly concerned about the copies lost in the old contract.

value_updates.replacement_contract_state: start fresh with new NFTs and prize draws
value_updates.legacy_contract_usage: leave deployed but exclude from active system use

execution.observed_behavior: Freelancer reports deploying the client-approved fresh-state replacement contract.

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text:
We have now switched to the new contract.
Could you confirm whether you can see any data on your dashboard, such as NFTs, tickets, etc.?

execution.observed_behavior: Freelancer reports that the system has been switched to the replacement contract.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Is this meant to balance the numbers because mint #1 didn’t include a ticket and commission?

If that’s the case, you can balance it if doing so is easy, although it isn’t required. It’s a one-off event that will only affect mint #1.

Do the contracts still need to be redeployed again? At the moment, everything appears to be working perfectly.

ambiguity.description: The client asks whether another contract redeployment is still required after the current behavior appears to work, leaving the redeployment decision unresolved.

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text: I now want us to safely redeploy the current changes to our existing smart contract without impacting the current users, NFTs, etc. We won’t use our existing deployer wallet since it will hold our data. I’ll share a new temporary deployer wallet, and then we can merge the changes now
